key_insight: A human–AI discovery loop produced the five-parameter Generalized Boyd algorithm, eliminating degree-skipping when constructing irreducible integer polynomials with small Mahler measure.
engineering_relevance: The work demonstrates how fast numerical exploration, distributed computing, and exact symbolic verification can support reliable AI-assisted mathematical discovery.
method: Use an AI agent to prototype numerical and symbolic solvers.
Run parallel searches across distributed clusters.
Collaboratively extract hypotheses and verify candidate polynomials exactly.
evidence_signal: Across all even degrees up to 2000, the approach improves six previously published values and holds 99.6% of best-known records; the authors release a verified polynomial dataset.
watch_item: The reported evaluation covers even degrees up to 2000; these computational records do not resolve Lehmer’s problem.
paper_title: Breaking the high-degree barrier in Lehmer's problem with a human-AI discovery loop
